articles.title: Single-Dose Psychedelic Nasal Spray Eases Treatment-Resistant Depression in JAMA Trial
articles.excerpt: In a 193-person phase 2b trial, one intranasal dose of mebufotenin cut depression scores by 5.3 points more than a near-zero control dose at four weeks — with the psychedelic effect over in about an hour.
articles.image_caption: A nasal spray delivery device. A JAMA trial found a single dose of a psychedelic nasal spray eased treatment-resistant depression.
articles.nri_angle: Treatment-resistant depression affects about 30% of people with major depression; a one-visit treatment, if later trials confirm it, would matter to patients who cannot manage the repeated clinic visits current alternatives require.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Stroke Is Striking Younger Adults, and Every Minute of Delay Costs Brain
articles.excerpt: On World Stroke Day, doctors in Hyderabad and Delhi warn cases in under-45s have risen 40-50%, younger patients are now 20-30% of all strokes, and 1.9 million brain cells die per minute untreated.
articles.image_caption: A World Stroke Day graphic shows a stylised brain over a world map for October 29. Doctors used the day to warn that stroke cases are rising in adults under 45 and that treatment is time-critical.
articles.nri_angle: For diaspora readers, the actionable core is universal: learn BE FAST, call 911 in the US at the first sign, and push parents in India toward regular blood-pressure checks — the risk factors are arriving a generation earlier on both sides.

articles.title: Air Pollution Can Harm Your Kidneys Too, Nephrologists Warn
